findings.title: Direct pattern-matching capture can rebind GGUF_IMAGE without being detected
findings.scope: The frozen current launcher is correctly selected; the defect is the claimed unambiguous binding guard for a concrete future syntactic rebind, not arbitrary Python runtime immutability.
findings.observed: Both expected-refusal fixtures exit 0 and qualify the original literal although a tiny isolated match-capture reproducer proves the inserted direct binding selects a different immutable image.
findings.recommendation: Account for direct pattern-capture binders (MatchAs, MatchStar and MatchMapping.rest as applicable) or explicitly restrict the supported source shape and fail closed. Do not import/execute the launcher or promise arbitrary runtime immutability.

findings.title: Success receipt is emitted before a required receipt write can fail
findings.observed: A synthetic storage failure produces process exit 1 / IsADirectoryError, but the already-emitted final receipt says final_exit=0 and status=qualified-native-amd64-prerequisites. The job is red; the success receipt is false.
findings.recommendation: Resolve required receipt storage first, catch its errors while preserving a prior primary failure, and emit a final nonqualification receipt consistent with the actual exit.

findings.title: Timeout handling stops after the group leader exits, leaving a TERM-resistant group member
findings.observed: The owned synthetic Popen leader exits on TERM; wait returns and breaks before group KILL. A same-group descendant that ignores TERM survives controller return and writes a later owned fixture marker. Primary exit 124 and Docker absence receipt remain nonzero/truthful; host CLI group drainage is not established.
findings.scope: Concrete synthetic controller-lifetime counterexample, not evidence that actual Docker forks this child or that a real container leaked. No guessed PID/PGID was signaled by the test; the bounded fixture reaches its natural completion point.
findings.recommendation: Keep an owned lifetime anchor while terminating/draining the command group. Do not fix this with a delayed unanchored killpg after the leader has been reaped, because that can target a recycled group ID.
